scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to make my 7-year-old brother go to sleep when he stayed up late watching a movie with my friend. Let me break this down step by step. First, my brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough, he gets all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep to function properly. Last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to handle things. I made sure my brother went to bed on time, but then my friend came over, and we started goofing around and watching a movie. We were kind of loud, and my brother woke up and wanted to join us. I told him to go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother all hyped up, and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed, it would lead to a big fight, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. So, I let him stay on the couch with us. By the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, my brother was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed. It was midnight, so he missed out on a couple of hours of sleep. The next morning, he didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he's not allowed to sleep past 8. He was pretty cranky. My mom found out and got mad at me. She said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad. I think since he's 7, he should know about consequences and understand that if he stays up later, he won't feel good the next day. I also told her that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? Let's think about this. On one hand, I was trying to avoid a big fight and keep things peaceful. I didn't want to deal with the stress of dragging him upstairs and having him throw a fit. Plus, my friend was over, and I wanted to keep things fun and not have my brother be upset. On the other hand, my brother's sleep is really important for his well-being. Missing out on sleep can affect his mood, behavior, and ability to function the next day. Even though he's 7, he should start learning about consequences and responsibilities, like understanding that staying up late can make him feel bad the next day. I also told my mom that two hours of missed sleep wasn't a big deal, but I'm not sure if that's accurate. I think for a 7-year-old, sleep is crucial, and missing out on even a couple of hours could have noticeable effects. Another thing to consider is the example I'm setting. If I let him stay up late, he might think it's okay to do it again, and it could become a habit. It's important to set boundaries and stick to routines, especially for younger kids who need structure. But then again, I was in a tough spot. My mom trusted me to handle things, and I didn't want to ruin the fun with my friend. It's a balance between being responsible and being a big brother who wants to have fun with his friends. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have set some limits with my friend to keep things quieter so my brother wouldn't have woken up in the first place. Or, if he did wake up, maybe I could have found a way to include him without letting him stay up too late. Overall, I think it's important to prioritize my brother's well-being, even if it means dealing with some short-term inconvenience. Teaching him about consequences and maintaining a consistent routine is probably more important in the long run. But I also don't want to be too strict or overbearing. It's a balance between being responsible and allowing some flexibility for fun and learning experiences. In the end, I think I should have stuck to the bedtime routine, even if it meant dealing with some resistance from my brother. It's better for his health and helps him understand the importance of sleep and responsibility.
